# Draft:Zhang Er (Han dynasty politician)

|p=Zhāng Ěr |w=Chang Erh}}
Zhang Er  (died 202 BCE) was born in Daliang , the capital of Wei. In his youth he was a youxia under the patronage of Lord Xinling, one of the Four Lords of the Warring States, but fled to Waihuang () county}} after committing some crimes.
In Waihuang, Zhang Er married the daughter of a local rich citizen, and was able to set himself up with his own group of followers, eventually becoming magistrate of Waihuang in the early days of the Qin empire. Zhang Er was close friends with  , and also knew Liu Bang in his commoner days, who often visited him.
Zhang Er joined the Chen Sheng and Wu Guang uprising against the Qin in 209 BCE. He was installed as King of Changshan () by Xiang Yu in 206 BCE, during the short-lived Eighteen Kingdoms period of the Chu-Han Contention. Having switched allegiance to Liu Bang, Zhang Er was installed as King of Zhao in 203 BCE. His son Zhang Ao succeeded him on his death in 202 BCE.
